attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, stated as fact.

semantics.note: Context ties 'the whole project' to OpenAI's Rubik's cube robotics work. The timing 'a year or two later' is kept.

contract.note: Reading 'dropped' as ending the research and 'quietly' as low-profile, disclosed later, is an ordinary reading. The 2020–2021 window follows from the 2019 demo.

evidence.note: TechCrunch (July 2021) reports OpenAI quietly disbanded the robotics team. It dates the decision to October 2020 and quotes the company saying it stopped robotics research.
OpenAI's October 2019 announcement sets the date of the demo. October 2020 is about a year later.

reviews.rationale: Reporting at the time says OpenAI decided in October 2020 to stop robotics research and refocus the team. Journalists only reported it in July 2021, which fits 'quietly'. October 2020 is about a year after the October 2019 demo, so the claim holds.

attribution.note: Marcus's own firm prediction ('I promise you').

semantics.note: 'I promise you' is firm language, so this is a scored forecast. The reasoning part of the sentence is handled in a separate claim. 'In the fullness of time' sets no deadline.

contract.note: Reading 'Gemini' as the original generation and 'same ballpark' as broadly comparable is reasonable. But the result depends on these readings and on 'untethered', which the speaker never defined.

evidence.note: An independent coding benchmark finds Gemini Ultra and GPT-4 close, each ahead in different settings. That is one domain only and says nothing about factual reliability.
Tests Gemini Pro only. It shows hallucinations, and Pro lagging GPT-4 in medicine. The contract bars treating Pro results as evidence about Ultra.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was given, so the claim can only resolve early through a broad set of independent evaluations that agree. The packet has one coding benchmark on Ultra and one medical study on Pro. Together they do not show both broad comparability with GPT-4 and persistent factual unreliability for the same model.

attribution.note: Marcus's own firm prediction ('I promise you').

semantics.note: Firm forecast with no deadline. The proposition faithfully keeps the reasoning and world-understanding part of the sentence.

contract.note: The readings of 'dicey' and 'very limited understanding' are fair and ordinary. They have no thresholds, so the result depends on interpretation.

evidence.note: Independent tests find Gemini Pro's reasoning weakens on longer, more complex questions. This covers Pro only and does not show unpredictability or failure on novel tasks.
Finds Gemini competitive at commonsense reasoning, with some weaknesses. This cuts against a sweeping 'very limited' but covers Pro only, and contamination is not controlled.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was given, and the rule for early resolution is not met. Both studies cover Pro models only, and their findings point in opposite directions. Neither controls for overlap with training data, and neither tests novel world-understanding tasks broadly.

attribution.note: Marcus's own retrospective statement in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps both parts: the cube had sensors and was modified, and the approach found little real-world application.

contract.note: Requiring both parts and separating deployment from research influence is fair. 'A whole lot' has no threshold.

evidence.note: OpenAI's technical paper says most experiments used a customised Giiker cube with built-in sensors. This supports the hardware part only.
The OpenAI blog also describes a vision-only setup using a cube with modified stickers. The cube was still not off the shelf, but not every result relied on sensors.

reviews.rationale: The hardware part holds: most experiments used a sensor-equipped cube, and even the vision-only cube was modified. The packet has no deployment records or retrospective on real-world use through December 2023, so the claim as a whole is not settled.
